To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MegaMIMO enables independent access points to beamform their transmissions and communicate with their wireless clients on the same wireless channel as if they formed one large MIMO system, and that MegaMIMO can provide a linear increase in wireless throughput with an increase in access points.
MegaMIMO is able to provide a throughput increase of 8.5× over a 10 AP system with 802.11g clients and 9.4 × over a 10AP system with 802,11n clients.
MegaMIMO is an efficient and scalable joint multi-user beamformer that allows multiple APs to share the same channel, and that it can be implemented with unmodified 11n cards.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of a novel multi-user beamforming architecture for wireless LANs.
the design of scalable wireless LANs that can support dense user demands.

the following questions: How can we scale the capacity of a wireless LAN by increasing the number of APs? How do we enable multiple APs to beamform their transmissions to their clients? How do we ensure that APs are able to beamform without interfering with each other?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MegaMIMO provides a significant improvement over existing wireless LAN systems in terms of throughput, fairness, and scalability.
MegaMIMO can be used to scale the throughput of an 802.11 network by adding more APs to the same channel.
MegaMIMO is an innovative and practical approach to scale the throughput of 802.11 networks by adding more access points.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MegaMIMO is an enabling technology to scale the throughput of a wireless LAN by adding more APs to it, and that it can provide significant performance gains even with commodity 802.11 hardware.
we show that the capacity of a wireless network can be scaled linearly with the number of access points by using joint multi-user beamformers.
we have demonstrated a 10-antenna system that can achieve 10x the throughput of a 1-antenna system in a congested deployment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the throughput of a wireless LAN can be scaled by adding more APs, without the need to change the channel or the MAC protocol.
the capacity of a wireless channel can be increased by orders of magnitude with the addition of more APs on a single channel, and that this can be done with unmodified 11n cards.
by exploiting spatial reuse and joint beamforming, it is possible to scale the capacity of wireless networks to support a large number of users.
